subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that pauses or aborts active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or should default steering remain boundary-based?
rationale: The choice changes shared runtime semantics, channel UX, Codex/native runtime integration, and compatibility with existing steer, followup, collect, and interrupt modes.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported default and use the narrower active-run admission issues only to make messages reach existing boundary-based steering reliably.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, fallback, and channel ingress.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steering as the supported default and limit related work to making messages reliably reach the existing model-boundary queue.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger lifecycle only after maintainer-approved compatibility proof across supported runtimes and channels.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, fallback, and channel ingress.
